skills.title: Body Systems and Their Jobs
skills.description: Your body has systems like digestive, respiratory, circulatory, nervous, and skeletal that each do a job. Can you match each system to what it does?

skills.title: Vital Organs
skills.description: Organs like the heart, lungs, brain, stomach, and intestines each have a shape and a job. Can you label each organ and pick what it does?

skills.title: Body Systems Work Together
skills.description: Body systems team up, like lungs and heart moving oxygen around your body. Can you pick how two systems help each other?

skills.title: Diseases and Body Systems
skills.description: Some diseases and disorders, like asthma, diabetes, and heart disease, affect certain organs or systems. Can you match each one to the part it affects?

skills.title: What Affects Our Health
skills.description: Things like sleep, air quality, friends, and exercise can help or hurt your health. Can you pick which ones help and which ones harm?

skills.title: Technology and Our Health
skills.description: Technologies like vaccines, screens, and fitness trackers can help or harm our bodies. Can you pick the good and bad effects?

skills.title: Food Choices and Health
skills.description: Reading food labels and knowing what foods are made of helps us choose foods that are good for our bodies and minds. Can you pick the healthy choice?

skills.title: Matter: Mass and Volume
skills.description: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Can you pick which things are matter?

skills.title: Solids, Liquids, and Gases
skills.description: Solids keep their shape, liquids take the shape of their container, and gases spread out to fill space. Can you sort matter and pick its properties?

skills.title: Changes of State
skills.description: Melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing, and boiling change matter from one state to another. Can you match each change to an example at home or outside?

skills.title: Heat and Changes of State
skills.description: Matter changes state when it takes in or lets go of heat energy. Can you pick whether heat goes in or out?

skills.title: Physical Changes
skills.description: In a physical change, matter changes state, size, or shape but stays the same substance, like cutting paper or dissolving sugar. Can you spot physical changes?

skills.title: Chemical Changes
skills.description: In a chemical change, a new substance forms. Signs are new colour, gas bubbles, heat or light, and a new smell. Can you spot chemical changes?

skills.title: Properties Make Matter Useful
skills.description: Properties like hardness, flexibility, and being able to flow make solids, liquids, and gases good for certain jobs. Can you match each material to its use?

skills.title: Making Products: Impacts
skills.description: Factories use steps like heating, cutting, and mixing to make products, and these affect people and nature. Can you pick the good and bad effects?

skills.title: Materials and the Environment
skills.description: The materials used in products, like plastic, metal, and paper, affect nature in different ways. Can you pick actions that lessen the harm?

skills.title: Forces Inside Structures
skills.description: Inside a structure, forces like compression, tension, torsion, and shear push, pull, twist, and slide its parts. Can you match each force to its effect?

skills.title: Forces Outside Structures
skills.description: Forces from outside, like loads, wind, and wave pushes, act on structures. Can you pick what each outside force does?

skills.title: Structures Against Nature's Forces
skills.description: Earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, and snow loads can damage buildings. Features like strong frames and sloped roofs help them hold up. Can you match each hazard to a helpful feature?

skills.title: Plants and Animals Handle Forces
skills.description: Turtle shells, bendy tree trunks, and strong bones help living things survive forces. Can you match each feature to how it protects?

skills.title: Protective Equipment
skills.description: Helmets, pads, and harnesses spread out or soak up forces to keep people safe. Can you match each gear to how it protects?

skills.title: Nature's Forces and Structures
skills.description: Natural events like floods, erosion, and storms affect buildings, bridges, and animal homes. Can you pick the effects?

skills.title: Protecting Communities From Forces
skills.description: Towns use things like dikes, stilts, and strong building rules to protect structures. Can you pick the best way for a city, farm, or remote community?

skills.title: Forms of Energy
skills.description: Energy comes in forms like light, sound, heat, electrical, chemical, and motion. Can you match each form to how we use it?

skills.title: Energy Is Never Lost
skills.description: Energy can't be made or destroyed. It only changes from one form to another. Can you pick the energy change in each example?

skills.title: Stored Energy in Devices
skills.description: Energy can be stored, like in a stretched spring or a battery, and then changed into motion or other forms. Can you follow the energy in a device?

skills.title: Wasted Energy
skills.description: When energy changes form, some escapes as heat, light, or sound that we can't use. Can you pick where the extra energy goes?

skills.title: Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy
skills.description: Sun, wind, and water energy keep coming back, but coal, oil, and gas run out. Can you sort the energy sources?

skills.title: Fossil Fuels and Climate Change
skills.description: Burning fossil fuels puts extra carbon dioxide in the air, which traps heat and warms Earth. Can you put the steps in order?

skills.title: Using Energy and Resources Wisely
skills.description: How people use energy and resources affects climate, nature, and society for a long time. Can you pick the long-term effects and ways to lessen them?

skills.title: Technology That Saves Energy
skills.description: Tools like LED bulbs, smart thermostats, and timers can cut the energy we use. Can you pick which technology saves the most energy?

skills.title: Indigenous Ways of Conserving
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities use traditional knowledge to take only what is needed and care for the land. Can you match each practice to how it saves resources?
